set.body:
Source: 2026-07-25 review finding 3. Narrow, immediately-closable subset of P6f.12.

Problem:
AgentDomainJson.scala:1694-1716 uses circe deriveEncoder/deriveDecoder for InvocationResult, JobRef, AcceptanceUncertainty, Submission, SubmissionAttempt, CancellationResult, CancellationAttempt, CapabilitySupport, SchedulerCapabilities, and SchedulerQueryResult. circe-generic emits {"CaseName": {...}}, so Scala case names are the wire contract. docs/compatibility.md states derivation alone is not a durable contract.

Only observation-timing-v1.json pins any of it (Succeeded, Observed, Current, CommandStdout). Grepping every fixture finds no "Accepted", "Rejected", "AcceptanceUnknown", "SpawnFailed" or "Acknowledged". Renaming any of those cases is a silent wire break that sbt test, mimaReportBinaryIssues, and scalafmtCheckAll all pass.

Acceptance (this bead):
- Byte-exact provenance-stamped golden fixtures covering every case of Submission, SubmissionAttempt, InvocationResult, CancellationResult, CancellationAttempt, AcceptanceUncertainty, SpawnFailureKind, CapabilitySupport, SchedulerCapabilities, and SchedulerQueryResult Empty/InvocationFailed/ParseFailed.
- Tests assert encode-to-fixture and fixture-to-decode, so a case rename fails CI.
- P6f.12 remains open for replacing derivation with owned codecs; this bead only removes the silent-break window.
set.title: P6f.30: Pin the derived agent wire shapes with golden fixtures
